message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on most highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is illegal.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – Cell Phone Use | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %).
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at stop signs; yield at yield signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, roundabouts, and intersections. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or low visibility.
• Fog lights only when visibility < 200 ft. | TxDOT – Headlights | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must be registered and display valid license plates.
• Towing regulations: minimum towing speed, brake requirements. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) – Registration | | **Parking Rules** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking on the right side of the road is prohibited in many areas. | TxDOT – Parking | | **School Bus Laws** | • All vehicles must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• No passing on either side of the bus. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not change lanes in a “no‑change” zone. | TxDOT – Lane Changing | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red means stop, green means go, yellow means slow down.
• Stop signs, yield signs, and traffic lights are mandatory. | TxDOT – Traffic Signals | | **Vehicle Safety Equipment** | • Must have working brakes, tires, lights, horn, and mirrors.
• Airbags must be functional. | TxDOT – Vehicle Safety | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | TxDMV – Insurance | | **Special Situations** | • **Construction Zones**: Follow posted signs and reduced speed limits.
• **High‑way Interchanges**: Use proper lane discipline.
• **Emergency Vehicles**: Yield to police, ambulance, and fire trucks. | TxDOT – Construction & Interchange Guidelines | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Regular updates on road conditions, construction, and new regulations. 3. **TxDMV** – For licensing, registration, and insurance requirements. 4. **Local County Courts** – For recent changes or local ordinances that may supplement state law. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular maintenance reduces accidents. - **Use hands‑free devices** – stay focused on the road. - **Be extra cautious in school zones** – speeds drop significantly. - **Check for construction signs** – they often require lane changes or reduced speeds. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law, recent changes, or how to handle a particular driving scenario!
